headline: Comparative genomics links gene copy number and selection to insect and dog traits
label: Comparative Functional Genomics Inference
summary: Genome-scale sampling across 275 insect genomes and two canine datasets now allows direct tests of selection and receptor diversity.
synthesis: The dominant thread is comparative and population-scale inference of functional and evolutionary structure from genomic sequence. A comparative analysis of C- and I-type lysozyme gene copy number across 275 insect genomes uses phylogenetic generalized least squares to relate copy number to feeding ecology, reporting few diet-linked patterns. A polygenic adaptation test, PolyGraph, applied to two canine genomic datasets of 1,987 and 722 dogs, detects early, shared selection on pro-social behavior during dog domestication. A third study maps 115 insect odorant receptors through combined sequence, structural, and docking-profile analysis, flagging a conserved Orco β-sheet. What is new here is the application of these inference frameworks to gene family dynamics, polygenic selection, and receptor structure across insect and canine systems.
